experiments.guard: WIRING: clicking a tab in the rail must switch tabs — the entire point of the drawer->modal rewrite. Both suites call window.chela.selectSettingsTab(...) directly and never dispatch a click on a rendered .settings-tab, so the onclick the user actually hits is exercised by nothing. After this mutation every tab click is a no-op (selectSettingsTab('') fails the SETTINGS_TABS membership check and returns) while the rail still renders and still highlights whatever the tests select programmatically.

nav.js's own comment: "focus: 'notify' opens straight to the Notifications tab (the popover's 'Notifications' row uses this)". topbarmenu.test.mjs only asserts the popover's onclick STRING is chela.toggleSettings('notify'); nothing asserts where that lands now that the panels are hidden per-tab (pre-CMX-287 it was a scrollTop on one long scroll, so the section was visible either way). After this mutation the bell opens on the last/default tab and the notification settings are not reachable from it at all.

notes: The round-3 verdict's third finding (settings_cost.test.mjs style.css '.settings-tabpanel { display: none }' -> '{ display: flex }') is deliberately NOT included here. It is not omitted by oversight: the orchestrator (PR #358, round-4 comment) ruled it an unfair test measured against this suite — tests/settings_cost.test.mjs never loads style.css and jsdom resolves no layout/box model, so no CSS mutation of any spelling can redden this suite; a stylesheet-text parser to fake a signal is the exact race CMX-117 already burned ~4 judge rounds on with correct code throughout. Closed instead by narrowing the test's docstring to state the gap explicitly (NOT GUARDED) and removing the 'or the CSS selector drifts' claim it could not back up. See docs/DEFEAT_SHAPES.md shape 5's third 'Found' entry for the two mutations that ARE guarded here.
